newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK foreign reserves US$62.1 bln at end Sept - HKMA.
newsitem.headline: HK foreign reserves US$62.1 bln at end Sept - HKMA.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said the amount of foreign currency assets held by the Exchange Fund, including unsettled forward transactions, amounted to US$62.1 billion at the end of September 1996.

This represents an increase of 8.6 percent or US$4.9 billion over the position at the end of December 1995 and an increase of 3.5 percent or US$2.1 billion in the third quarter, said the HKMA, the territory's de facto central bank.
Net foreign currency forward transactions outstanding at the end of September amounted to US$6.7 billion, it said.

The figure was relatively high due to swap transactions during the third quarter to meet market intervention needs and seasonal drawdowns of fiscal reserves from the Exchange Fund by the government, the HKMA said.
If forward transactions were excluded, the amount of foreign currency assets in the Exchange Fund, used to back the Hong Kong dollar, at the end of September would stand at US$55.4 billion, it noted.
That would be the same level as recorded at the end of December 1995 but 3.3 percent less than that at the end of June 1996, reflecting seasonal drawdowns of fiscal reserves, it said.
